evidence.heading: Actions / Artifacts and reinforcements
evidence.text: Artifacts are not encounter cards. Follow each artifact's printed effect, permitted role and timing; normally discard after play. **Any player, including an uninvolved bystander, may play Cosmic Zap** on an otherwise legal power use. It cancels that use, including your own, and prevents further uses for that encounter. Cards that cancel cards follow their own printed instructions.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Original fifty alien reference / Philanthropist
evidence.text: **FAQ pp6,18:** The given card can be seen before the immediate Cosmic Zap decision. With Philanthropist Super, defense must play the given card and cannot invoke general timing to avoid it. A power loan using Philanthropist Wild includes associated holdings such as Miser's hoard.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Original fifty alien reference / Vulch
evidence.text: **FAQ p21:** You cannot salvage the Cosmic Zap that zapped you: your use remains canceled when it is discarded. Artifacts discarded by a player using Vulch Wild against you remain eligible, potentially passing back and forth. Play Vulch Super on the first eligible flare discard; it then lasts for all eligible flare discards during the encounter, but cannot retrieve itself.

evidence.heading: Actions / Flare system
evidence.text: Return a flare to hand **immediately after its effect finishes**, rather than discard it, unless its effect states otherwise. A player may play **at most one flare per encounter**, and an individual flare can be used **only once per encounter even if it changes hands**. A Card Zap targeting the flare counts against the player's limit. Prevention of play differs from cancellation after play: see Anti-Matter's FAQ exception. If a Super enables a power use, that power can still be Cosmic Zapped even outside its usual role/phase. The flare remains in hand rather than being discarded or forced to Wild; Only Wild is available for an otherwise legal play while the power is zapped. Zapping the enabled power does not undo the already-played flare or permit a second play of it in the same encounter; the ordinary per-player and per-flare limits still apply. When your own Wild would otherwise be handed to your alien, keep it after resolution.

evidence.heading: Player Reference
evidence.text:
| Step | Main task |
|---|---|
| Start Turn, first encounter only | Replace encounter-less offensive hand before Regroup effects |
| Regroup | Mandatory one-ship warp retrieval if available |
| Destiny | Determine defense/system; reshuffle before drawing last card |
| Launch | Target planet and commit 1–4 offense ships normally |
| Alliance | Offense invites, defense invites, others commit clockwise |
| Planning | Main players select encounter cards; respect powers' before/after timing |
| Reveal | Reveal pairing, resolve effects and reinforcement responses |
| Resolution | Ship destinations, compensation/rewards, discards, victory check |

evidence.heading: Turn Structure / 2. Destiny
evidence.text:
- Another player's color: encounter that player in their home system.
- Your own color: redraw, or target one chosen foreign colony in your home system, making its owner the defense. Other colonies there are bystanders. You can instead aim at a home planet with **no ships of any color**, moving up to four ships from other colonies there to reclaim it automatically. This counts as a win and successful encounter, proceeds only through Launch, and can qualify you for a second encounter.
- Wild: choose another player and encounter them in their home system.
- Special: follow its conditions, defense and location. The original rulebook's illustrated special card chooses the other player with the most current foreign colonies, excluding offense. Break a tie toward offense's left, choosing the first tied eligible player there; encounter that player in their home system (rulebook p7). For color-dependent effects such as Shadow, treat it as the designated defense's color.

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Original fifty alien reference / Kamikaze
evidence.text: **FAQ p16:** Choose and sacrifice all ships for a use together before drawing, rather than one at a time while inspecting draws. Play Kamikaze Super anew each encounter in which its effect is wanted.

evidence.heading: Turn Structure
evidence.text: The original rulebook lists seven encounter phases in order: **Regroup, Destiny, Launch, Alliance, Planning, Reveal, Resolution**. The first encounter also has the Start Turn step before Regroup effects.

#### Barbarian

**Loot and Pillage — Offense only; mandatory; Resolution.**

- After winning an encounter, before compensation (if any) collected, use power to loot opponent's cards.
- Take and look at opponent's hand. For each of your ships in encounter, may choose one card from that hand and add it to own.
- Afterwards discard remainder of opponent's hand.

evidence.heading: Oracle
evidence.quote:
#### Oracle

**Foresee — Main player only; mandatory; Planning.**

- Before encounter cards selected, force opponent to play encounter card FACEUP.
- Only after seeing opponent's card select and play own card.

**Rulebook p14; FAQ p18; FAQ p6:** Against Sorcerer, foresee first: Sorcerer plays faceup, then Oracle chooses facedown; after both are selected Sorcerer can switch them. Against Gambler, Gambler must reveal or bluff before Oracle chooses. In the official Oracle Wild example, play the flare faceup in front of you outside the hands, mix the hands together, take your new hand at random from the mixed cards, then return the flare to hand when its effect finishes.

- Before encounter cards selected may trade hands with opponent. Both then keep new hands.

evidence.heading: Fido
evidence.quote:
#### Fido

**Fetch — As any player; optional; Resolution.**

- After encounter cards discarded at end of encounter, may retrieve one of those discarded cards and offer to another player.
- If refused, may keep it. If accepted, other player keeps it, then you may either retrieve one ship from warp or draw one card from deck.

**FAQ p13; FAQ p4:** Take only an actual encounter card played as such, not an encounter card merely discarded by Plague, Fodder or Reserve. evidence.heading: Chosen
evidence.quote:
#### Chosen

**Divine Intervention — Main player only; optional; Reveal.**

- After revealing encounter cards, may pray for divine intervention once per encounter: draw three cards from deck.
- If none are encounter cards discard them, no further effect. If any are encounter cards may choose one to replace own revealed encounter card (discard replaced card).
- If own revealed card and chosen replacement are both attacks, may instead add chosen card value to revealed attack value, or replace as normal.
- Discard all other drawn cards; resolve encounter with new card or card value.

**FAQ pp7,11:** You can be Cosmic Zapped after the cards are drawn and your intended choice is known, within the immediate same-phase zap window. Chosen Super is played after inspecting the drawn cards.

evidence.heading: 5. Planning
evidence.quote:
### 5. Planning

Each main player selects an **encounter card**—attack, negotiate or Morph—and places it facedown. Allies do not play encounter cards. Resolve applicable powers at their stated before/after-selection timing; a phase label does not erase that timing. Defense replaces an encounter-less hand as described above. Offense cannot normally replace its hand now.

- When not offense, before destiny chosen, use power to take destiny deck, look through it and choose any card; played as though offense had drawn it.
- On own turn, or any time zapped, remaining destiny cards shuffled and one dealt randomly.
